dedupe_keys.name: tullstorp stream restoration and multifunctional wetlands for agricultural water storage sweden

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes how landowners along the 30 km Tullstorp stream in Skåne, southern Sweden, restored a channelised stream and built multifunctional wetlands to cope with both floods and droughts in an area where farmland covers 85% of the basin. The first project, started in 2009 by the Tullstorp Stream Economic Association, re-meandered and re-naturalised the riverbed and created flood storage areas, buffer strips and wetlands; by 2021 over 50 wetlands totalling 200 ha had been created or restored and 25 km of stream restored, cutting nitrogen by 30% and phosphorus by 50%. After the wet and dry years of 2017 to 2019, Tullstorp stream 2.0 (from 2019) added multifunctional water reservoirs, recirculating irrigation and customised drainage so that excess water stored in wet periods can be used in droughts. The page is free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal, drawing on the EEA 2021 report on nature-based solutions. Caveats: funding remains a challenge, benefits are reported by the project, and the 2.0 pilots were still under way. It illustrates adaptation planning with blue-green infrastructure for rural drainage and water supply; a related record is the Oppla nature-based solutions repository.
name: Tullstorp stream restoration and multifunctional wetlands for agricultural water storage (Sweden)
outcomes: Over 50 wetlands (200 ha) created or restored and 25 km of stream restored by 2021, with nitrogen down 30% and phosphorus down 50%; a second phase stores wet-season water for drought use.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study on the Tullstorp Stream Economic Association
resources_used: recirculating irrigation and customised drainage pilots
